# Mastery Assessments

Assess a major topic with several forms of evidence. A score is descriptive;
it does not by itself establish durable mastery.

## Suggested weighting

| Assessment area | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Conceptual understanding | 20% |
| Technical knowledge | 20% |
| Practical implementation | 30% |
| Problem solving | 20% |
| Real-world application | 10% |

## Descriptive score bands

| Score | Interpretation |
|---:|---|
| 0-49 | Foundation not established |
| 50-69 | Developing |
| 70-79 | Competent |
| 80-89 | Advanced |
| 90-100 | Mastery demonstrated |

An 80% score is a suggested pass threshold, not a guarantee. A mastery claim
also requires demonstrated practical implementation and independent reasoning.
Revisit and retest weak prerequisites before dependent advanced topics.

## Exam evidence

Use a balanced selection of:

- Concept explanation and prerequisite checks.
- Technical recall applied to a novel example.
- Coding, SQL, calculation, debugging, or data interpretation.
- An unfamiliar scenario requiring method selection and justification.
- Limits, assumptions, validation, and trade-offs.

In interactive mode, ask one question at a time. Share the rubric before or
after the exam as appropriate, but do not reveal answers before the learner's
attempt. Record topic, date, evidence, score, status, strengths, and gaps.
Clearly label any component that was not executed or independently verified.
